summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted with altered mental status, worsening abdominal and back pain, and signs of infection including fever, tachycardia, and hypotension. She had recently been treated for C. difficile infection and was no longer taking lubiprostone. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and mild transaminitis, but imaging revealed no acute abdominal process, ascites, or source of infection. Blood cultures remained negative, and the C. difficile test was cancelled due to formed stool. She was treated with IV fluids and ceftriaxone for presumed sepsis, with improvement in mental status on lactulose for hepatic encephalopathy. Antibiotics were transitioned to oral levofloxacin for completion at home. Her pain was attributed to chronic IBS and a stable T10 paraspinal mass. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved cognition, and a plan to start linaclotide after insurance approval, with close follow-up arranged.
